source.title: Common-agency Games for Multi-Objective Test-Time Alignment
source.authors: Bai-Ting Chen; Tong Zhu; Ruihan Yu; Xiao-Wu Dai

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses 7B reward models to guide a larger frozen model at test time as part of its own multi-objective alignment method. It reports that method's performance, but does not test the fine-tuning-on-weak-labels effect or its PGR.
record.gate_note: The weak-to-strong extension guides frozen Alpaca-65B with 7B reward models at inference. It does not fine-tune the stronger model on labels, report the weak supervisor's task performance, compare against an Alpaca-65B true-label ceiling, or calculate PGR. The 65B HV/MIP results are recorded as findings about this different test-time setup, not as evidence for a claim version.
record.test_reason: The 'weak-to-strong extension' uses 7B reward models to guide frozen Alpaca-65B at decoding time. It reports only CAGE's HV/MIP against other test-time methods (GenARM, PARM). There is no fine-tuning of a strong model on weak labels, no weak-supervisor score, no strong true-label ceiling and no PGR. It borrows the term and reports its own method's performance (T4).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors claim CAGE is a training-free multi-objective test-time alignment method that beats GenARM, PARM and MOD. They say 7B reward signals can guide Alpaca-65B, which they call weak-to-strong alignment capability. They report no weak-supervisor or ceiling comparison.
record.recipe_differences: The original claim concerns fine-tuning a strong model on weak-model labels. This paper keeps the base model frozen and uses reward-model signals for test-time guidance.

fits_no_version.finding: With 7B reward models guiding frozen Alpaca-65B at test time, CAGE gets HV 356.32 and MIP 0.828, against GenARM 262.23/0.722 and PARM 221.96/0.657 (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small reward models can steer a larger frozen model at decoding time, and equilibrium aggregation beats linear logit blending on multi-objective metrics.

record.problems: For the weak-to-strong extension, the paper reports aggregate multi-objective metrics against other alignment methods, not a weak-supervisor score or a strong-model true-label ceiling. It gives no uncertainty estimates for these results.
record.rows_left_out: The GenARM and PARM values in Table 2 are comparator results for alternative test-time guidance methods, not measurements of the fine-tuning-on-weak-labels claim. Other tables and figures concern different model/task settings or unrelated multi-objective results.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on weak labels, weak-supervisor performance, strong ceiling or PGR.
No auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling or loss variants evaluated for PGR.
Only one size pairing (7B guidance, 65B base), and no PGR measured.
No exploitation, distribution-shift or shared-error tests.
The theory concerns equilibrium existence, stability and regret, not when a student must beat its supervisor.

record.verdict_notes: Weak-to-strong is used in a loose sense (small reward model guiding a larger model at decoding). This is not the fine-tuning-on-weak-labels paradigm. Preprint; no uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on weak-model labels, weak-supervisor score, strong true-label ceiling, or PGR.
No auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensembling, or loss-variant comparison for raising PGR.
The paper reports one larger-model reward-guidance setting, but does not measure PGR or its variation with supervisor/student size, task, or representations.
No tests of supervisor-checking failures, distribution shift, or shared error patterns.
No theory of when a student must outperform its supervisor.

rows.subject: Alpaca-65B
rows.operation_detail: CAGE applies test-time reward guidance from 7B reward models to the frozen larger base model.
rows.note: Reports CAGE's result in the weak-reward-model-to-larger-model test-time setting. HV does not establish whether a fine-tuned student beats its weak supervisor or measure PGR.
rows.check: Method-comparison row: CAGE vs GenARM/PARM HV on 65B. The baselines are alternative methods, not a weak supervisor or a strong ceiling, so no PGR can be computed. Keep it as a fits_no_version finding only.

rows.subject: Alpaca-65B
rows.operation_detail: CAGE applies test-time reward guidance from 7B reward models to the frozen larger base model.
rows.note: Reports CAGE's result in the weak-reward-model-to-larger-model test-time setting. MIP does not establish whether a fine-tuned student beats its weak supervisor or measure PGR.
rows.check: Same as r1, for MIP. The study's own method is compared with others, which says nothing on whether a student beats its supervisor.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
